params.body:
The Netwerk graph was a flat picture of relations only. Most dots carried no name, because names were drawn for a fixed top list, and nothing opened when you clicked a dot except the side panel. This rebuilds it the way graph explorers (Neo4j Bloom, Linkurious, Kumu) work: start from an overview, click to open neighbours, show names by priority without overlap, and offer a 3D view to turn around.

## What changes for the user

- **Two kinds of dots.** Relations are round (coloured by role or group, as before). Projects are dark squares.
- **Click to open.** Clicking a relation opens its projects in the period around it, linked with a dashed line, and opens its panel as before. Clicking a project opens the relations on it. Clicking an open dot again closes what it opened. At most 25 open per click (the most recent projects, or the busiest relations), with "N meer niet getoond" below the graph. "Alles sluiten" goes back to the overview.
- **Names.** The focus (hovered or selected dot) is always named, then its neighbours, then opened dots, high importance and the busiest relations, as long as a name does not overlap another one. Smaller dots get their name as you zoom in. The names stay the same size on screen.
- **3D.** A 3D button switches to a three.js view you turn by dragging (orbit controls). Clicking opens there too. Only the important dots carry a name in 3D, because names cannot step aside there. Dragging a dot is off in 3D: it conflicts with the orbit controls (3d-force-graph throws on release) and a drag in 3D is for turning.
- Opened dots, positions and the 2D/3D choice survive a redraw of the page, so saving a tag does not reset the picture.

The 2D turn buttons from #69 are gone: in 2D the layout has no up or down, and in 3D turning is the main gesture.

## Code

- `force-graph` (canvas) replaces the hand-written SVG simulation. `3d-force-graph` and `three-spritetext` are imported dynamically, so three.js (about 1.3 MB) loads only when someone presses 3D. `d3-force-3d` adds a collide force so dots do not overlap.
- `resources/js/network-model.js`: the parts without a screen (`merge` of the overview and what was opened, `pickLabels` for non-overlapping names), tested in Node.
- `Network::expand($id, $from, $until, $max)`: a relation gives its projects (label, last date, number of relations on it); a project (`p:` prefix) gives its relations (role, group, importance, project count). Undated project contacts count through a dated project, as in `contacts()`.
- `Network` component: `expand()` is `#[Renderless]`, so a click fetches data without redrawing the page. The graph's `wire:key` no longer contains the selection; the graph follows `selected` through `$wire.$watch`, so a click in the side panel centres that dot.

## Tests

- `NetworkTest`: a relation opens its projects in the period only, labelled and sized, with `more` when capped; a project opens its relations busiest first, including the undated architect; the page answers `expand`. 12 tests.
- `tests/js/network-model.test.js`: opened parts merge once; what hangs off a closed dot disappears; names never overlap except the focus.
- Full suite 229/229, JS 13/13, pint clean. Checked in headless Chromium on a local database with sample data: open a relation (25 projects appear around it), open a project, zoom in for names, switch to 3D and turn it, with no page errors.
